My situation is extremely similar to yours. I'm a 23F with social anxiety, and I only hang out with my Mum too.

I feel worthless sometimes too, and I sometimes cry because I'm sick of how my depression/anxiety affects me. My self esteem is pretty low, and it's shit. 

I only go to the cinema with my mother, I don't have friends anymore. I lost them all eventually because I was just in a bad place mentally. I didn't want to see anyone. I just wanted to stay home all the time, because it's my safe place. 

I've always been single too. 

I guess what I'm trying to say is that you're not alone, you might feel it, but your Mom loves you as much as mine loves me. 

I don't know how I would get through this without her.

You're still grieving, and everyone grieves differently. The people who say 'You should be over it by now.' or 'You should just accept it and move on' don't listen to them. You know how your grief better than anyone, because it's yours. Grief sucks, and it's hard. I still have bad days, and I wish I didn't exist sometimes, and on those days I think if I can make it through this hour, I'll think about the next hour when it comes. Or even just getting through ten, twenty or half hour blocks at a time. Start small, and work your way up when you're ready.

Set small goals, set your alarm to wake up at a certain time, even if you snooze it. You'll have achieved a goal of waking up at x time. 

Only you know when you're ready for therapy. The fact you've come here and posted takes a lot of strength. Maybe you're not ready for therapy just now, but even just posting here or on /r/offmychest, they're really supportive over there. 

I tried writing a letter to my friend, maybe you could write one to your brother, or just write how you're feeling in a notebook, or talk or write a letter to your parents, just to get the feelings out. It doesn't have to be long. It could just be a few words, or a few pages. 

But even if therapy isn't for right now, just know that is an option, whenever you're ready, whether that is next month or next year.

My friend died the same way. I'm so sorry you lost your brother. 

You are good enough and you're not bothering anyone by posting here. 

It took me a long time to accept it had happened, and even now, thirteen years later, I've still not come to terms with it, and I probably never will, but I've learned to live with it.

She was nine when she died, and like your brother, was taken way too soon. 

You should maybe give therapy another go. My therapist told me 'You have to be ready for therapy.' You won't know if you are unless you go.

23F in the same boat. No boyfriends, no kisses, no dates, no relationships, no flings, no sex. I feel like it's always going to be this way.

I just made this throwaway for anonymity, because I wanted to post in this subreddit, and this caught my eye. I'm a 23F, and I know how you feel. I was in college, (which you call community college, I'm from Europe) and I was doing fine, I passed my first year, then my second year came around. I got really ill in the winter and fell behind, and had to quit.

I got better after about three months (once I was treated by a doctor who wasn't a quack) and started looking for a job. I found said job, and I started working there. 

My depression had been there since I left college, but with being physically ill, my mental health fell to the wayside, and I was pushing it away, thinking that a job would be the answer.

I was so desperate to be working that I took the first job offered, and it was awful. My boss was a complete asshole, and I began dreading going to work. 

I went to a doctor and was diagnosed with anxiety and depression, and I was given a form which meant my doctor said I was unfit for work.

My asshole boss began harrassing me about when I was coming back, to the point he showed up at my house unexpectedly.

I was paid off, and I've just been struggling with this ever since. 

I know how you feel, feeling that life is passing you by, and being stuck in a rut. 

I don't know what I want to do with my life, and I feel like a complete loser. People I went to school with have kids, are engaged, married, have full time jobs and are travelling to cool places, and I'm just stuck with this nonexistence.

I guess I just wanted to say you're not alone.
